He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UTSA Roadrunners men's basketball|UTSA Roadrunners]]. ==High school career== Wallace played basketball for [[Richardson High School]] in [[Richardson, Texas]].{{cite web |last=Briggs |first=Jerry |title=Wallace's coach in high school recalls a fierce work ethic |url=https://thejbreplay.com/wallaces-coach-in-high-school-recalls-a-fierce-work-ethic |website=The JB Replay |access-date=July 31, 2021 |date=February 25, 2021}} As a senior, he averaged 22.2 points, 4.6 assists and 3.9 rebounds per game, earning District 9-6A Offensive Player of the Year honors.{{cite web |title=Keaton Wallace - 2020-21 - Men's Basketball |url=https://goutsa.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/keaton-wallace/5606 |website=UTSA Athletics |access-date=July 31, 2021 |archive-date=July 28, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210728124746/https://goutsa.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/keaton-wallace/5606 |url-status=dead }} ==College career== As a freshman at [[UTSA Roadrunners men's basketball|UTSA]], Wallace averaged 11.4 points, 3.1 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game, and was named to the [[Conference USA]] All-Freshman Team.{{cite web |last=Luca |first=Greg |title=As Jackson continues recovery, UTSA prepares for season opener |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/college_sports/local_colleges/article/As-Jackson-continues-recovery-UTSA-prepares-for-13364426.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=August 2, 2021 |date=November 5, 2018}} Entering his sophomore season, he gained about {{cvt|20|lb}} of muscle from the start of his college career and became an improved scorer.{{cite web |last=Luca |first=Greg |title=After adding muscle, Wallace stepping forward as top scorer for UTSA |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/college_sports/utsa/article/After-adding-muscle-Wallace-stepping-forward-as-13469002.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=July 31, 2021 |date=December 14, 2018}} Wallace formed the highest-scoring backcourt in nation with [[Jhivvan Jackson]].{{cite web |last=Luca |first=Greg |title=UTSA seniors Jhivvan Jackson, Keaton Wallace ready for final run at Conference USA tournament |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/colleges/utsa/article/UTSA-seniors-Jhivvan-Jackson-Keaton-Wallace-16013135.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=August 2, 2021 |date=March 9, 2021}} On February 2, 2019, he recorded a career-high 45 points, the fourth most in a game in program history, and seven rebounds in a 116–106 win against [[Marshall Thundering Herd men's basketball|Marshall]].{{cite web |title=Wallace scores 45 as UTSA beats Marshall in overtime |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/college_sports/utsa/article/Wallace-scores-45-as-UTSA-beats-Marshall-in-13584656.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=August 3, 2021 |date=February 2, 2019}} As a sophomore, Wallace averaged 20.2 points, five rebounds and 2.4 assists per game, receiving Second Team All-Conference USA honors.{{cite web |last=Newton |first=Cameron |title=The UTSA Roadrunners have the country's most electric scoring duo |url=https://www.midmajormadness.com/2019/10/2/20894312/utsa-roadrunners-countrys-best-scoring-duo-jhivvan-jackson-keaton-wallace-cusa-basketball-ncaa-hoops |website=Mid-Major Madness |access-date=August 3, 2021 |date=October 2, 2019}} He set a program single-season record with 121 three-pointers.{{cite web |last=Maenius |first=Julia |title=Athlete of the Week: Keaton Wallace |url=https://paisano-online.com/22703/sports/athlete-of-the-week-keaton-wallace/ |website=[[The Paisano]] |access-date=July 31, 2021 |date=February 4, 2020}} On December 3, 2019, Wallace posted a junior season-high 31 points, nine rebounds and five assists in an 89–67 win over [[Texas A&M–Corpus Christi Islanders men's basketball|Texas A&M–Corpus Christi]]. He recorded the most free throws without a miss (15) in program history.{{cite web |title=Wallace scores 31 to lift UTSA past Texas A&M-CC 89-67 |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2019/12/03/wallace-scores-31-to-lift-utsa-past-texas-am-cc-89-67/40758003/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=August 3, 2021 |date=December 3, 2019}} As a junior, Wallace averaged 18.8 points, 4.5 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game, repeating on the Second Team All-Conference USA.{{cite web |last=Luca |first=Greg |title=Jhivvan Jackson, Keaton Wallace return to top form as UTSA beats UTEP |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/college_sports/utsa/article/Jhivvan-Jackson-Keaton-Wallace-return-to-top-15907284.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=August 3, 2021 |date=January 28, 2021}} On February 5, 2021, he recorded a senior season-high 33 points and seven rebounds in an 87–80 win against [[FIU Panthers men's basketball|FIU]].{{cite web |title=Wallace explodes in win at FIU on Friday night in Miami |url=https://goutsa.com/news/2021/2/5/mens-basketball-recap-at-fiu.aspx |website=UTSA Athletics |access-date=August 3, 2021 |date=February 5, 2021}} As a senior, Wallace averaged 16.8 points, 5.5 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game, and was named to the Second Team All-Conference USA for a third time. He left as the second-leading scorer in program history behind Jhivvan Jackson. Wallace declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his additional year of college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Luca |first=Greg |title=NBA draft day arrives for UTSA hopefuls Keaton Wallace, Jhivvan Jackson |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/colleges/utsa/article/NBA-draft-UTSA-Keaton-Wallace-Jhivvan-Jackson-16347028.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=August 3, 2021 |date=July 28, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Agua Caliente / Ontario Clippers (2021–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Wallace joined the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|first=Greg|last=Luca|title=Former UTSA guard Keaton Wallace joining Memphis Grizzlies for NBA Summer League|url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/colleges/utsa/article/Former-UTSA-guard-Keaton-Wallace-joining-Memphis-16353117.php|work=[[San Antonio Express-News]]|date=July 30, 2021|access-date=July 31, 2021}} He was selected with the ninth pick of the second round of the [[2021 NBA G League draft (October)|2021 NBA G League draft]] by the [[Wisconsin Herd]]{{cite web |date=October 23, 2021 |title=Keaton Wallace picked in NBA G League Draft |url=https://goutsa.com/news/2021/10/23/mens-basketball-keaton-wallace-picked-in-nba-g-league-draft.aspx |access-date=October 30, 2021 |work=[[UTSA Roadrunners]]}} and subsequently traded to the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]], joining the team on October 27.{{cite web|title=Agua Caliente Clippers announce training camp roster for 2021-22 NBA G League season|url=https://aguacaliente.gleague.nba.com/agua-caliente-clippers-announce-training-camp-roster-for-2021-22-nba-g-league-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2021|access-date=October 31, 2021|archive-date=October 29, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211029180145/https://aguacaliente.gleague.nba.com/agua-caliente-clippers-announce-training-camp-roster-for-2021-22-nba-g-league-season/|url-status=dead}} On February 21, 2023, Wallace agreed to a two-way contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|title=Keaton Wallace: Joins Clippers on two-way contract|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-keaton-wallace-joins-clippers-on-two-way-pact/|website=CBSSports.com|date=February 21, 2023|access-date=February 21, 2023}} He was waived by the Clippers on March 1, without having played a game at the NBA level.{{cite tweet|first=Tomer|last=Azarly|title=The LA Clippers have waived Keaton Wallace, the team has announced.|number=1631103589815926784|user=TomerAzarly|date=March 1, 2023|access-date=March 2, 2023}} On March 4, 2023, Wallace was reacquired by the [[Ontario Clippers]].{{cite web|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=NBA.com|date=March 4, 2023|access-date=March 4, 2023}} ===Atlanta Hawks / College Park Skyhawks (2023–2026)=== On August 31, 2023, Wallace's rights were traded to the [[College Park Skyhawks]]{{cite web|title=College Park Skyhawks Acquire Returning Player Rights to Keaton Wallace and Brandon Randolph in Separate Deals|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/college-park-skyhawks-acquire-returning-player-rights-to-keaton-wallace-and-brandon-randolph-in-separate-deals/n-6008713|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=August 31, 2023|access-date=August 31, 2023}} and on September 29, he signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Guards Jarkel Joiner and Keaton Wallace|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-guards-jarkel-joiner-and-keaton-wallace|website=NBA.com|date=September 29, 2023|access-date=September 29, 2023}} However, he was waived on October 8.{{cite tweet|first=Lauren L.|last=Williams|title=Not huge surprise here but the Hawks have waived Jarkel Joiner and Keaton Wallace. Both guys were on Exhibit 10 deals. They’ll likely head to the Skyhawks.|number=1711117662837707236|user=WilliamsLaurenL|date=October 8, 2023|access-date=October 8, 2023}} On October 29, he joined the College Park Skyhawks.{{cite web|title=College Park Skyhawks Finalize Training Camp Schedule and Roster|url=https://cpskyhawks.gleague.nba.com/news/college-park-skyhawks-finalize-training-camp-schedule-and-roster-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=November 10, 2023}} On July 15, 2024, Wallace signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Hawks.{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Guard Keaton Wallace to a Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-guard-keaton-wallace-to-a-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2024|access-date=July 15, 2024}} Three years after going undrafted, Wallace finally made his NBA debut on October 27, 2024 in a 104 - 128 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] where he recorded 2 points and 1 rebound in 3 minutes of playing time.{{Cite web |title=Hawks vs Thunder, October 27, 2024 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202410270OKC.html |access-date=2025-12-06 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} On January 15, 2025, Wallace scored a career-high 27 points in a 110-94 win against the Chicago Bulls.{{cite web|url= https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/keaton-wallace-scores-career-high-27-points-to-help-the-hawks-beat-the-bulls-110-94/|title= Keaton Wallace scores career-high 27 points to help the Hawks beat the Bulls, 110-94|website=CBS Sports|date=January 15, 2025|access-date=April 13, 2025}} On April 13, Wallace recorded his first career triple-double, scoring 15 points, grabbing 11 rebounds, and recording 15 assists in a 117–105 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/atlanta-hawks/hawks-news-quin-snyder-reacts-historic-triple-double-finish-regular-season|title=Hawks' Quin Snyder reacts to historic triple-double to finish regular season|website=ClutchPoints|last=Brown|first=Malik|date=April 13, 2025|access-date=April 13, 2025}} He made 31 total appearances (five starts) for Atlanta during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 5.4 points, 1.6 rebounds, and 2.6 assists. On October 18, 2025, the Hawks converted Wallace's two-way contract into a standard contract.{{Cite web|title=Hawks convert two-way player, sign wing to open two-way spot|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/2025/10/hawks-convert-two-way-player-sign-wing-to-open-two-way-spot/|access-date=October 24, 2025|website=ajc.com|language=en}} === Maccabi Tel Aviv BC
